Card.signature: Card(children: (Text | Markdown | Link | Metric | Avatar | AvatarStack | Heading | LeadingText | EntityTitle | ImageTitle | Callout | CodeBlock | Image | ImageGallery | Separator | HorizontalBarChart | RadarChart | PieChart | RadialChart | SingleStackedBarChart | ScatterChart | AreaChart | BarChart | LineChart | Table | TagBlock | Form | Buttons | IconButton | Steps | Timeline | Checklist | EntityList | EditableTable | ValueCard | ValueLayout | InsightCard | CompositeCardBlock | ImageCard | Tabs | Carousel | Stack | Section | Grid | Shell | Bleed)[], variant?: "outlined" | "lifted" | "sunk", title?: string, subtitle?: string)
Card.description: Styled container, never borderless. variant: "outlined" (default, a thin border on a transparent background) | "lifted" (white, with the same border plus a soft shadow, to raise it off the page) | "sunk" (a light grey fill, no border or shadow, for a recessed group). Use "outlined" for ordinary groups such as a chart or a set of KPIs; "lifted" sparingly, for the one block that should stand out, such as a recommended option or a summary; "sunk" for secondary or nested content, such as a card inside another card or supporting notes. There is no borderless Card: to group content without a frame, use Stack (or Section for a part of the response). Never put a Table or EditableTable inside a Card: a table draws its own frame, so a Card around it doubles the border. Place it directly in a Section, TabItem or AccordionItem, with a Heading or Text title above it if it needs one. Optional title and subtitle (3rd and 4th, after variant) render as the card's own small header, 14px over 13px secondary like our other cards; use them instead of a Heading child, e.g. Card([chart], null, "Revenue by quarter", "USD thousands"). Always full width. Children stack top to bottom by default; to customise the layout (a row, a wrap, other gaps), pass a single Stack as the child, e.g. Card([Stack([a, b], "row")]). Cards flex to share space in a row Stack.

Text.description: Short UI text: labels, headings, captions, single values. variant: "small" | "default" (single-line UI text), "body" (a few lines of supporting copy, 16px on a 24px line) or "h1" | "h2" | "h3" (headings). emphasis: true sets non-heading text in Medium weight. Text is for building UI; for explanations, titled prose answers, or anything with lists, tables or several paragraphs, use Markdown (with # headings) instead.

Markdown.description: Long-form markdown prose: explanations, summaries and the top-level text that sets context around UI. Supports headings, lists, task lists, tables, quotes and code. When an answer needs a title, start the Markdown with a # heading instead of a separate Text heading. Not for short UI labels or single values; use Text for those.

Metric.signature: Metric(value: string, delta?: string, variant?: "horizontal" | "vertical", size?: "sm" | "default" | "large", previous?: string)
Metric.description: A value with an optional change, e.g. Metric("$48,200", "+8.1%"): a leading +/- on the change shows a green up or red down arrow. It has no label: in a Card give it the Card's title, and elsewhere compose one with Text or Heading. Metric uses the UI font, so its size follows its role: use size "sm" (14px) whenever it is not the hero number, which covers Table cells, EntityListItem right, ListItem and EntityTitle subtitles, ImageTitle content, the value of a horizontal ValueCard, and CompositeCardItem body (a CompositeCardItem footer price always renders at 18px), e.g. Col("Revenue", @Each(data.rows, "r", Metric(r.revenue, r.change, "horizontal", "sm"))) or EntityListItem("Trail Runner", Metric("$89", null, null, "sm")). Use "large" (18px) with variant "vertical" only for a standalone headline figure such as a KPI tile, Card([Metric("$48,200", "+8.1%", "vertical", "large")], null, "Revenue"); "default" (16px) is for a headline figure that sits inline. variant "horizontal" (default) puts the change beside the value, "vertical" under it. previous is an earlier value shown struck through after the current one; use it only for a real before/after, like a price drop or a revised figure, e.g. Metric("$89", "-26%", null, "sm", "$120"), and leave it out otherwise.

Avatar.signature: Avatar(name: string, src?: string, shape?: "circle" | "rounded", domain?: string, size?: "inline" | "md" | "lg", icon?: Icon | Shape, color?: "neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "purple" | "pink" | "inverted")
Avatar.description: A small real image that can stand in for an Icon: a person's photo or a company logo. Avatar(name, src?, shape?, domain?, size?, icon?, color?). People: Avatar("Ada Lovelace", "https://…/ada.jpg", null, null, null, Icon("user", "people")) is a circle (default). Companies: Avatar("Stripe", null, "rounded", "stripe.com", null, Icon("building-2", "business")) shows the site's logo from its domain. ALWAYS pass an icon, even with src or domain: it renders when the image is missing or broken (without one a generic placeholder shows). Without an image, an Icon inside and a color tint make a badge: Avatar("Billing", null, "rounded", null, "md", Icon("credit-card", "finance"), "info"); color "neutral" (default) | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "purple" | "pink" | "inverted". src must be a real URL from a tool result or the user; never invent one, pass the domain or an Icon instead. Pass only a domain you know is that company's own site. Which to use: a company is an Avatar with its domain; a person is an Avatar with src only when you have a real photo URL for them, otherwise Avatar("Ada Lovelace", null, null, null, null, Icon("user", "people")) with no src; a concept shown as a standalone tinted badge (size md or lg, e.g. leading a row or card) is an Avatar with icon and color; an icon on a text line (LeadingText, Tag, Chips) for a concept is a plain Icon. Pick color by meaning like Tag variants (success positive, danger negative, warning caution, info informational, neutral otherwise); use purple and pink only to tell categories apart. size "inline" (default, sits on a text line like an Icon) | "md" 32px | "lg" 48px for standalone use.

Emoji.description: A single emoji sized like an Icon, for a touch of expression in generated content: Emoji("🎉", "Celebration"). It fills the leading slot of a LeadingText or the icon of a Callout and never stands alone; for an emoji inside a sentence, type it in the Markdown text. Use it rarely, at most one or two per response, in content where it adds tone an Icon can't, e.g. Callout("success", "**You're all set!** Your trip is booked.", null, Emoji("🎉")) or LeadingText(Emoji("🌸"), Text("Cherry blossom season peaks in early April")). Never in UI chrome: dashboards, forms, tables, data rows, buttons, statuses and navigation use Icon. Don't stack several or use one to repeat what the text says. label is the accessible name; omit it when the emoji is decorative.

Shape.description: A small solid shape sized like an Icon. It only goes inside a Tag, a LeadingText or an Avatar's icon slot, never on its own. Use it where a plain colored mark says more than a picture: a status dot, Tag("Online", Shape("circle", "success")); a legend or category marker, LeadingText(Shape("square", "purple"), Text("Design")); or a trend arrow, LeadingText(Shape("triangle-up", "success"), Text("+12% this week")) or triangle-down with "danger". Use an Icon instead when the mark has to depict something. shape "circle" | "square" | "diamond" | "triangle-up" | "triangle-down" | "triangle-left" | "triangle-right" | "hexagon". color is "neutral" (default) | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "purple" | "pink" | "inverted", picked by meaning like Tag variants, with purple and pink for telling categories apart; keep one meaning per color within a response. label is the accessible name: give one when the shape carries meaning without text beside it, omit it when decorative.

AvatarStack.description: Several Avatars overlapped left to right, for a group of real people or companies: a team, attendees, who replied, investors in a round. AvatarStack([a1, a2, a3, a4, a5], 3) shows three and a "2" count chip. Use it for 2 or more; a single one is an Avatar. max caps how many show, keep it 3–5. size "inline" | "md" (default) | "lg" applies to every avatar, so set it on the stack, not on each Avatar. Each Avatar follows the Avatar rules: a real photo src or a company domain, and always an icon. A stack does not say who is in it, so name the group in Text beside it, usually with LeadingText.

Heading.description: A title with an optional one-line description under it, for titling a UI section such as a card group, chart or form. Most titles need no description. Add one only when it carries a fact the title lacks (a scope, unit, time range or what to do), e.g. Heading("Top products", "By units sold, last 30 days"). Never use it to greet, introduce yourself, restate the title or say what the section contains: not Heading("Hello!", "I'm your AI assistant"), not Heading("Revenue", "Revenue overview"). size "default" (a section title inside a response) | "lg" (a hero title at the top of a page). Use Heading when a title needs that supporting line; use Text h1/h2/h3 for a bare title, and Markdown # headings for titled prose answers.

LeadingText.signature: LeadingText(leading: Icon | Avatar | AvatarStack | Emoji | Shape, text: Text, tone?: "primary" | "secondary")
LeadingText.description: A leading visual in front of any Text, centered on its first line and scaled to the Text variant. leading is an Icon, an Avatar or an AvatarStack. Which to lead with: a concept, fact or status (a date, place, price, check) is an Icon, e.g. LeadingText(Icon("calendar", "time"), Text("Opens daily 9am–6pm")); one specific person or company is an Avatar, e.g. LeadingText(Avatar("Stripe", null, "rounded", "stripe.com", "inline", Icon("building-2", "business")), Text("Stripe")); a group of people or companies (a team, attendees, who replied) is an AvatarStack, e.g. LeadingText(AvatarStack([a1, a2, a3, a4], 3, "inline"), Text("Ada, Grace and 2 others")). Keep avatars at size "inline" here so they sit on the text line. tone "secondary" mutes both. Icon names must be exact kebab-case lucide names; an unknown name renders a plain circle.

EntityTitle.signature: EntityTitle(leading: Avatar | Icon | Emoji, title: string, subtitle: string | Text | Metric | Tag | TagBlock | LeadingText | Link | (string | Text | Metric | Tag | TagBlock | LeadingText | Link)[], layout?: "horizontal" | "vertical")
EntityTitle.description: A leading visual with a title and a one-line subtitle, naming a person, company, product, place or topic, e.g. EntityTitle(Avatar("Stripe", null, "rounded", "stripe.com", null, Icon("building-2", "business")), "Stripe", "Payments infrastructure"). leading is usually an Avatar: a photo (src) for a person you have a real photo URL for, a logo (domain, shape "rounded") for a company, or a tinted icon badge (icon, color) for anything else. A bare Icon renders as a neutral badge; an Emoji also works in rare expressive content. leading is 44px, or 48px in the vertical layout; the title is 16px medium. subtitle is required. A string is one line of secondary context such as a role, category or time range. To say more on that line, compose it: a Tag for a status (EntityTitle(Avatar("Ada Lovelace", null, null, null, null, Icon("user", "people")), "Ada Lovelace", Tag("On call", null, "success"))), a Metric for a price or value with its change (Metric("$29", "-12%", null, "sm")), a Link for a source (Link("stripe.com", "https://stripe.com")), a TagBlock for a few labels, or a LeadingText for a fact with an icon. If there is nothing useful to put under the title, use LeadingText instead. Use it standalone for a list of people, companies or places, and in a CompositeCardItem header to say what the card is about. Use Heading for a section title over UI. layout "vertical" stacks the leading above the text, for narrow grid cards. When the subtitle needs two or more pieces side by side, pass them as an array and they sit on one line, e.g. [Metric("$89", null, null, "sm"), Tag("In stock", null, "success")]; a single piece goes in directly.

ImageTitle.signature: ImageTitle(image: Image, content: (Text | Heading | EntityTitle | LeadingText | Metric | Tag | TagBlock | Link | (Text | Heading | EntityTitle | LeadingText | Metric | Tag | TagBlock | Link)[])[])
ImageTitle.description: An Image with a short content stack under it, for one item in a set of products, articles, places or listings: ImageTitle(Image("Trail Runner shoe", "https://…/trail.jpg", "1:1"), [Text("Trail Runner", "body", true), Metric("$89", "-26%", null, "sm", "$120")]). content is usually two parts: a title, as Text(title, "body", true), then one secondary line. The image is already the visual, so never put an EntityTitle with an icon Avatar under it; use an EntityTitle only for a real person, brand or seller with their own photo or logo, such as a host or a store. For a place or thing, use the Text title, a secondary line such as LeadingText(Icon("map-pin", "travel"), Text("Kyoto, Japan"), "secondary"), and Tags. For an article that line is the author, inline with a very small avatar: LeadingText(Avatar("Ada Lovelace", null, null, null, "inline", Icon("user", "people")), Text("Ada Lovelace · 6 min read"), "secondary"). For a product it is a price Metric (with previous for a sale); for a place, a Tag, TagBlock or a short secondary Text. Keep it to 2–3 parts; longer copy belongs in Markdown. Use ImageTitle for 2 or more comparable items side by side in a grid or as Carousel slides, one Card per item (Carousel([Card([item1]), Card([item2]), Card([item3])])), giving every item the same parts in the same order and the same Image aspectRatio ("1:1" products, "4:3" places, "16:9" articles). For a single picture that illustrates an answer, use Image with Markdown around it instead. The Image src must be a real URL from a tool result or the user; with no real image, use EntityTitle instead. When one line of content needs two or more pieces side by side, such as a price and a stock status, pass them as an array and they sit on one line: [Metric("$89", null, null, "sm"), Tag("In stock", null, "success")]; a single piece goes in directly.

Link.description: Standalone link to a web page, shown with the site's favicon before the text. text is a short descriptive label (a page or site name, never a bare URL); url is an absolute https URL from a tool result or the user, never invented. size "default" fits everywhere else; "lg" is for a Link used as the title of a ListItem, StepsItem or TimelineItem, matching the title text: Link("Install the SDK", "https://…", "lg"). For links inside sentences, use a Markdown [text](url) link instead.

Callout.signature: Callout(variant: "neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "purple" | "pink" | "inverted" | "error", content: string, visible?: $binding<boolean>, icon?: Icon | Emoji)
Callout.description: A Notion-style callout: an icon followed by Markdown content on a tinted block, with no title. Use it to make one important aside stand out from the answer around it: a tip, a caveat, a warning or the result of an action. Keep it to 1–3 sentences and lead with a short bold phrase when that helps, e.g. Callout("warning", "**Visa required.** Apply at least 3 weeks before you travel."). Use at most one or two per response; regular explanation belongs in Markdown. Pick variant by meaning, which also sets the tint and default icon: "info" context (info), "success" a positive result (circle-check), "warning" a caution (triangle-alert), "danger" a failure or risk (circle-x; "error" is an alias), "neutral" a tip (lightbulb), "purple" a highlight or something new (sparkles), "pink" something personal or loved (heart), "inverted" a high-emphasis note on a dark block (info). Most callouts are info, success, warning, danger or neutral; use purple, pink and inverted sparingly. Pass an Icon only when a more specific one helps, e.g. Callout("info", "Doors open at 7pm.", null, Icon("clock")). visible is an optional reactive $boolean for a toast: it auto-dismisses after 3s by setting $visible to false.

Image.description: Image with alt text and a URL. aspectRatio crops it to a fixed frame (default "3:2"): "1:1" for logos, avatars and product shots, "4:3" or "3:2" for photos, "16:9" for hero and video-like media, "3:4" or "9:16" for portraits and phone screenshots; "auto" keeps the image's own proportions (charts, diagrams, screenshots that must not be cropped).

ImageGallery.signature: ImageGallery(images: {src: string, alt?: string, details?: string}[])
ImageGallery.description: A grid of real photos the reader can open full size: ImageGallery([{ src, alt, details? }, ...]). Use it near the top of a visual answer (a venue, destination, style or product line) to show 3–9 photos at once; details is an optional caption in the preview. Only real image URLs from a tool result or the user, never invented. For photos that are options to pick, use ImageCard instead.

Table.description: Data table, column-oriented: Table([Col("Language", langs), Col("Users (M)", users, "number")]); each Col holds its own data array. It draws its own frame, so never wrap it in a Card (that doubles the border): place it directly in a Section, TabItem or AccordionItem, with a Heading or Text title above it if needed.

Col.description: Column definition — holds label + data array

EditableTable.signature: EditableTable(name?: string, columns?: EditableCol[], rows?: (string | number | any)[][])
EditableTable.description: Spreadsheet-like table the user edits inline: EditableTable(name, columns, rows), e.g. EditableTable("tasks", [EditableCol("task", "Task"), EditableCol("status", "Status", "select", [SelectItem("todo", "Todo"), SelectItem("done", "Done")]), EditableCol("due", "Due", "date")], [["Design review", "todo", "2026-10-12"]]). Each row is an array of values in column order (dates as ISO strings, selects as the SelectItem value). Edits are submitted as a form field named after the table when the user clicks Save Changes. It draws its own frame, so never wrap it in a Card; place it directly in a Section or TabItem.

EditableCol.signature: EditableCol(key: string, label: string, type?: "text" | "number" | "date" | "select" | "url", options?: SelectItem[], icon?: Icon, width?: number)
EditableCol.description: One EditableTable column: EditableCol(key, label, type?, options?, icon?, width?). type is the cell editor: "text" (default), "number", "date", "select" (pass options as SelectItems) or "url". icon is an optional leading header Icon; each type has its own default.

BarChart.signature: BarChart(labels: string[], series: Series[], variant?: "grouped" | "stacked", xLabel?: string, yLabel?: string, height?: number)
BarChart.description: Vertical bars; use for comparing values across categories with one or more series

LineChart.signature: LineChart(labels: string[], series: Series[], variant?: "linear" | "natural" | "step", xLabel?: string, yLabel?: string, height?: number)
LineChart.description: Lines over categories; use for trends and continuous data over time. A height of 120 or less draws a sparkline with no axes, legend or grid, scaled to the data, for a KPI Card.

AreaChart.signature: AreaChart(labels: string[], series: Series[], variant?: "linear" | "natural" | "step", xLabel?: string, yLabel?: string, height?: number)
AreaChart.description: Filled area under lines; use for cumulative totals or volume trends over time. A height of 120 or less draws a sparkline with no axes, legend or grid, scaled to the data, for a KPI Card.

RadarChart.description: Spider/web chart; use for comparing multiple variables across one or more entities

HorizontalBarChart.signature: HorizontalBarChart(labels: string[], series: Series[], variant?: "grouped" | "stacked", xLabel?: string, yLabel?: string)
HorizontalBarChart.description: Horizontal bars; prefer when category labels are long or for ranked lists

PieChart.signature: PieChart(labels: string[], values: number[], variant?: "pie" | "donut", appearance?: "circular" | "semiCircular")
PieChart.description: Circular slices; use plucked arrays: PieChart(data.categories, data.values)

RadialChart.description: Radial bars; use plucked arrays: RadialChart(data.categories, data.values)

SingleStackedBarChart.description: Single horizontal stacked bar; use plucked arrays: SingleStackedBarChart(data.categories, data.values)

Slice.description: One slice with label and numeric value

ScatterChart.signature: ScatterChart(datasets: ScatterSeries[], xLabel?: string, yLabel?: string)
ScatterChart.description: X/Y scatter plot; use for correlations, distributions, and clustering

Point.signature: Point(x: number, y: number, z?: number)

Form.signature: Form(name: string, buttons: Buttons, fields?: (FormControl | FormRow)[])
Form.description: Form container for essential input that cannot be picked from options, such as a name, an email, exact dates or free text: Form(name, buttons, fields), with one FormControl or FormRow per field and exactly one primary submit Button. Keep it to the fewest fields. When the user is choosing between options, offer tappable ImageCard or InsightCard tiles or Buttons instead of a Form.

FormRow.description: Puts 2–3 short, related FormControls side by side inside a Form, such as first and last name or city and postcode: FormRow([firstName, lastName]). The fields share the width equally and stack into one column when the Form is narrow. Mix FormRows with full-width FormControls in the same Form fields list; long fields like TextArea stay full width.

FormControl.signature: FormControl(label: string, input: Input | TextArea | Select | DatePicker | Slider | CheckBoxGroup | RadioGroup | Chips | OptionCards, hint?: string)
FormControl.description: Field with label, input component, and optional hint text

Input.signature: Input(name: string, placeholder?: string, type?: "text" | "email" | "password" | "number" | "url" | "search" | "tel", rules?: {required?: boolean, email?: boolean, url?: boolean, numeric?: boolean, min?: number, max?: number, minLength?: number, maxLength?: number, pattern?: string}, value?: $binding<string>, variant?: "default" | "inline")
Input.description: A single-line text field inside a FormControl: Input(name, placeholder?, type?, rules?, value?, variant?), e.g. Input("email", "you@example.com", "email", { required: true, email: true }). Pick type for what is being entered, "email" | "password" | "number" | "url" | "search" | "tel" or "text" (default), because it sets the leading icon and the keyboard automatically. placeholder shows an example value, not the label; the label goes on the FormControl. value binds a $variable for reactive filters such as Input("q", "Search tickets", "search", null, $search). variant "inline" is a borderless field (outlined only on hover or focus, with no leading icon) for table cells and dense rows; use "default" everywhere else. When the answer comes from a known set, prefer Select, DatePicker, Chips or OptionCards.

TextArea.signature: TextArea(name: string, placeholder?: string, rows?: number, rules?: {required?: boolean, email?: boolean, url?: boolean, numeric?: boolean, min?: number, max?: number, minLength?: number, maxLength?: number, pattern?: string}, value?: $binding<string>, variant?: "default" | "inline")
TextArea.description: A multi-line text field inside a FormControl, for free-form notes or messages: TextArea(name, placeholder?, rows?, rules?, value?, variant?), e.g. TextArea("notes", "Dietary needs, accessibility, special requests…", 4). rows sets the visible height; 3–5 is typical. Never require it when leaving it blank is a valid answer. variant "inline" is borderless until hover or focus, for table cells and dense rows; use "default" everywhere else. For a one-line answer use Input.

Select.signature: Select(name: string, items: SelectItem[], placeholder?: string, rules?: {required?: boolean, email?: boolean, url?: boolean, numeric?: boolean, min?: number, max?: number, minLength?: number, maxLength?: number, pattern?: string}, value?: $binding<string>, variant?: "default" | "inline")
Select.description: A dropdown of SelectItems inside a FormControl, for picking one option from four or more: Select(name, items, placeholder?, rules?, value?, variant?), e.g. Select("country", [SelectItem("us", "United States"), SelectItem("uk", "United Kingdom"), SelectItem("de", "Germany")], "Select…", { required: true }). For two or three options, RadioGroup or Chips show every choice at once. value binds a $variable, e.g. a sort field that drives @Sort. variant "inline" is borderless until hover or focus, for table cells and dense rows; use "default" everywhere else.

SelectItem.description: One option in a Select: SelectItem(value, label); value is what the form submits, label is what the user sees.

DatePicker.signature: DatePicker(name: string, mode?: "single" | "range", rules?: {required?: boolean, email?: boolean, url?: boolean, numeric?: boolean, min?: number, max?: number, minLength?: number, maxLength?: number, pattern?: string}, value?: $binding<any>, variant?: "default" | "inline")
DatePicker.description: A date field with a calendar inside a FormControl: DatePicker(name, mode?, rules?, value?, variant?), e.g. DatePicker("travel-dates", "range", { required: true }). mode "single" (default) picks one date; "range" picks a start and end, for trips, bookings or report periods. value binds a $variable. variant "inline" is borderless until hover or focus, for table cells and dense rows; use "default" everywhere else.

Slider.signature: Slider(name: string, variant: "continuous" | "discrete", min: number, max: number, step?: number, defaultValue?: number[], label?: string, rules?: {required?: boolean, email?: boolean, url?: boolean, numeric?: boolean, min?: number, max?: number, minLength?: number, maxLength?: number, pattern?: string}, value?: $binding<number[]>)
Slider.description: Numeric slider input; supports continuous and discrete (stepped) variants

CheckBoxGroup.signature: CheckBoxGroup(name: string, items: CheckBoxItem[], rules?: {required?: boolean, email?: boolean, url?: boolean, numeric?: boolean, min?: number, max?: number, minLength?: number, maxLength?: number, pattern?: string}, value?: $binding<Record<string, boolean>>)

CheckBoxItem.signature: CheckBoxItem(label: string, description: string, name: string, defaultChecked?: boolean)

RadioGroup.signature: RadioGroup(name: string, items: RadioItem[], defaultValue?: string, rules?: {required?: boolean, email?: boolean, url?: boolean, numeric?: boolean, min?: number, max?: number, minLength?: number, maxLength?: number, pattern?: string}, value?: $binding<string>)

RadioItem.signature: RadioItem(label: string, description: string, value: string)

SwitchGroup.signature: SwitchGroup(name: string, items: SwitchItem[], value?: $binding<Record<string, boolean>>)
SwitchGroup.description: A list of on/off switches inside a FormControl, for independent settings or preferences that each turn on or off: SwitchGroup(name, items, value?). value binds a $variable holding { name: boolean }. It has no frame of its own; put it in a Card when it needs one. To pick items from a list use CheckBoxGroup, and for one choice among several use RadioGroup.

SwitchItem.signature: SwitchItem(label?: string, description?: string, name: string, defaultChecked?: boolean)
SwitchItem.description: One toggle in a SwitchGroup: SwitchItem(label?, description?, name, defaultChecked?), e.g. SwitchItem("Email alerts", "Get a message when a build fails", "email-alerts", true). name is the key submitted with the form; description is an optional one-line explanation under the label; defaultChecked starts it on.

ChipItem.signature: ChipItem(value: string, label: string, leading?: Icon | Avatar | Emoji, disabled?: boolean)
ChipItem.description: One selectable pill: ChipItem(value, label, leading?, disabled?), e.g. ChipItem("hotel", "Hotel", Icon("building", "buildings")). label is 1–3 words; leading is an optional Icon, an Avatar for a person or company, or a rare Emoji. Give every chip a leading or none of them.

Chips.signature: Chips(name: string, type?: "single" | "multiple", items?: ChipItem[], rules?: {required?: boolean, email?: boolean, url?: boolean, numeric?: boolean, min?: number, max?: number, minLength?: number, maxLength?: number, pattern?: string}, defaultValue?: string | string[])
Chips.description: A form field of compact selectable pills, inside a FormControl, for choosing one or many short options: Chips(name, "single" | "multiple", [ChipItem(...), ...], rules?, defaultValue?). A selected chip shows a checkmark at the end. Use it for short labels (1–3 words) such as tags, amenities or tools; for choices that need a description use OptionCards. The selection is stored under `name`.

OptionCard.signature: OptionCard(value: string, title: string, subtitle?: string | Text | Metric | Tag | TagBlock | LeadingText | Link | (string | Text | Metric | Tag | TagBlock | LeadingText | Link)[], leading?: Icon | Avatar | Emoji | Image, disabled?: boolean)
OptionCard.description: One selectable card: OptionCard(value, title, subtitle?, leading?, disabled?), e.g. OptionCard("adventure", "Adventure", "Hiking, trekking & outdoor activities", Icon("mountain", "nature")). subtitle is one line of context: a string, or a Text, Metric, Tag, TagBlock, LeadingText or Link, or an array of them on one line, such as a price Metric for a plan. leading is an Icon for a concept, an Avatar for a person or company, a real Image, or a rare Emoji.

OptionCards.signature: OptionCards(name: string, type?: "single" | "multiple", items?: OptionCard[], rules?: {required?: boolean, email?: boolean, url?: boolean, numeric?: boolean, min?: number, max?: number, minLength?: number, maxLength?: number, pattern?: string}, defaultValue?: string | string[])
OptionCards.description: A form field of selectable cards in a responsive grid, inside a FormControl, for choosing one or many options that need a short explanation: OptionCards(name, "single" | "multiple", [OptionCard(...), ...], rules?). The selected card shows a checkmark. Use it for 2–6 meaningful choices such as a plan, trip type or working style; for many short labels use Chips, and for a long list use Select. Every card should have the same parts, all with a leading or none. The selection is stored under `name`.

Button.signature: Button(label: string, action?: ActionExpression, variant?: "primary" | "secondary" | "tertiary", type?: "normal" | "destructive", size?: "default" | "large", leading?: Icon)
Button.description: A pill button: Button(label, action?, variant?, type?, size?, leading?). The label says exactly what clicking does, e.g. Button("Book a table", @ToAssistant("Book a table at Septime"), "primary"). variant "primary" (solid, the one main action in a group) | "secondary" (supporting actions) | "tertiary" (lowest emphasis, e.g. "Skip"). type "destructive" (red) only for an action that deletes or cancels something. size "default" (32px) for almost every button; "large" (40px) only for a single prominent call to action, never for a row of buttons. Don't use the older "extra-small" | "small" | "medium" sizes. leading is an optional Icon before the label, added only where it clarifies the action (e.g. Icon("external-link") on a button that opens a site); most buttons have none.

IconButton.signature: IconButton(name: string, icon: Icon, action?: ActionExpression, variant?: "primary" | "secondary" | "tertiary", size?: "default" | "large")
IconButton.description: A round icon-only button: IconButton(name, icon, action?, variant?, size?). name is the accessible label and the action's label, so it must say what the click does, e.g. IconButton("Share", Icon("share-2"), @ToAssistant("Share this itinerary"), "secondary"). Use it only where the icon alone is unmistakable (share, close, more, next) and space is tight, like a card corner or a row of tools; anything less obvious needs a Button with a label. variant "primary" (solid) | "secondary" | "tertiary" (lowest emphasis, the usual choice). size "default" (32px) for almost every case; "large" (40px) only beside a large Button.

Stack.signature: Stack(children: any[], direction?: "row" | "column", gap?: "none" | "xs" | "s" | "m" | "l" | "xl" | "2xl", align?: "start" | "center" | "end" | "stretch" | "baseline", justify?: "start" | "center" | "end" | "between" | "around" | "evenly", wrap?: boolean)
Stack.description: Flex container. direction: "row"|"column" (default "column"). gap: "none"|"xs"|"s"|"m"|"l"|"xl"|"2xl" (default "m"). align: "start"|"center"|"end"|"stretch"|"baseline". justify: "start"|"center"|"end"|"between"|"around"|"evenly".

Section.signature: Section(children: (Text | Markdown | Link | Metric | Avatar | AvatarStack | Heading | LeadingText | EntityTitle | ImageTitle | Callout | CodeBlock | Image | ImageGallery | Separator | HorizontalBarChart | RadarChart | PieChart | RadialChart | SingleStackedBarChart | ScatterChart | AreaChart | BarChart | LineChart | Table | TagBlock | Form | Buttons | IconButton | Steps | Timeline | Checklist | EntityList | EditableTable | ValueCard | ValueLayout | InsightCard | CompositeCardBlock | ImageCard | Tabs | Carousel | Stack | Grid | Shell | Bleed | FollowUpBlock | Sources)[])
Section.description: One part of a response. Every response is built from Sections: put each distinct part (an overview, then options, then next steps) in its own Section, directly in the root, so parts get more space between them and their own children sit close together. A short single-part answer is one Section. Sections are high-level divisions, and many responses need only one: never give a lone Text, Markdown or Buttons row its own Section, nor a Section that holds only a title (a Heading or Text, with or without a subtitle; it goes at the top of the Section with the content it introduces), e.g. not Section([Markdown("Here is a snapshot…")]) followed by the table it introduces. Put an intro first inside the Section it introduces, and closing actions last in the final Section. Children stack top to bottom; compose the part yourself inside it: a Heading or Text h2/h3 title first when the part needs one, then Markdown, a Stack row or grid, a card block, a chart. Prose inside a titled Section is a Markdown block without its own # heading. e.g. Section([Heading("Where to stay"), hotels]). Never nest a Section inside a Section. For parts the reader opens on demand (an FAQ, a long report) use the collapsible SectionBlock inside a Section, and for alternative views of the same thing use Tabs.

Grid.signature: Grid(children: (Text | Markdown | Link | Metric | Avatar | AvatarStack | Heading | LeadingText | EntityTitle | ImageTitle | Callout | CodeBlock | Image | ImageGallery | Separator | HorizontalBarChart | RadarChart | PieChart | RadialChart | SingleStackedBarChart | ScatterChart | AreaChart | BarChart | LineChart | Table | TagBlock | Form | Buttons | IconButton | Steps | Timeline | Checklist | EntityList | EditableTable | ValueCard | ValueLayout | InsightCard | CompositeCardBlock | ImageCard | Card | Tabs | Carousel | Stack)[], columns?: 2 | 3 | 4)
Grid.description: Equal-width columns for dashboards: Grid(children, columns?). columns 2 (default) | 3 | 4 is the most at full width; narrower screens drop to fewer automatically, so never build rows by hand (4 steps down to 2, then 1; 3 and 2 step down to 1). Cells are 12px apart and stretch to the row's height. Fill each cell with one block, usually a Card (outlined by default), or a chart or a card block, and keep the cells of one Grid the same kind, titled with the Card's own title (not a Heading child), e.g. a KPI row Grid([Card([Metric("$48,200", "+8.1%")], null, "Revenue"), ...], 4) above a chart Grid([Card([chart1], null, "Revenue"), Card([chart2], null, "Orders")]). In a chat response the Card's title comes after sources and variant: Card([chart1], null, null, "Revenue"). For a row of mixed widths use a Stack row; for 2+ items of one card type use its card block.

Shell.signature: Shell(title: string, children: (Text | Markdown | Link | Metric | Avatar | AvatarStack | Heading | LeadingText | EntityTitle | ImageTitle | Callout | CodeBlock | Image | ImageGallery | Separator | HorizontalBarChart | RadarChart | PieChart | RadialChart | SingleStackedBarChart | ScatterChart | AreaChart | BarChart | LineChart | Table | TagBlock | Form | Buttons | IconButton | Steps | Timeline | Checklist | EntityList | EditableTable | ValueCard | ValueLayout | InsightCard | CompositeCardBlock | ImageCard | Card | Grid | Tabs | Carousel | Stack)[])
Shell.description: A frame for a dashboard or a large Grid composition: Shell(title, children). It shows a small title over its content, renders wider than the chat column, and has an expand button that opens the content full screen. title is a short name for what it shows (e.g. "Store performance, last 30 days"). Children stack top to bottom, usually one or two Grids of Cards. Use at most one Shell per response, only for dashboards and large Grid layouts; ordinary answers never need one.

Bleed.signature: Bleed(children: (Text | Markdown | Link | Metric | Avatar | AvatarStack | Heading | LeadingText | EntityTitle | ImageTitle | Callout | CodeBlock | Image | ImageGallery | Separator | HorizontalBarChart | RadarChart | PieChart | RadialChart | SingleStackedBarChart | ScatterChart | AreaChart | BarChart | LineChart | Table | TagBlock | Form | Buttons | IconButton | Steps | Timeline | Checklist | EntityList | EditableTable | ValueCard | ValueLayout | InsightCard | CompositeCardBlock | ImageCard | Card | Grid | Tabs | Carousel | Stack)[])
Bleed.description: Frameless content wider than the chat column, for expressive layouts: Bleed(children). Same breakout as Shell but with no header, outline or expand button; on narrow screens it just fills the column. Children stack top to bottom, 12px apart. Use it sparingly, for a part that benefits from width: a wide hero Image, a wide comparison Grid, an editorial layout or a wide Carousel, e.g. Bleed([Image("Lisbon at dusk", url, "16:9"), Grid([c1, c2, c3], 3)]). When a Grid must compare an odd number of cards side by side, such as 3 or 5 plans or options, wrap it in a Bleed so they sit in one wide row instead of wrapping into an uneven 2 + 1: Bleed([Grid([plan1, plan2, plan3], 3)]). Never nest a Bleed or Shell inside it; for a dashboard with an expand button use Shell.

Tabs.description: Pill tabs that switch between alternative views of the same thing, such as one dataset as a chart and a table, or the same plan by season: Tabs([tab1, tab2]). Only one view shows at a time, so never hide primary information that the reader needs to compare side by side in a tab. Keep it to 2–5 tabs with short labels. For distinct parts of a response use Sections, and for supplementary on-demand detail use Accordion.

TabItem.signature: TabItem(value: string, trigger: string, content: (Text | Markdown | Link | Metric | Avatar | AvatarStack | Heading | LeadingText | EntityTitle | ImageTitle | Callout | CodeBlock | Image | ImageGallery | Separator | HorizontalBarChart | RadarChart | PieChart | RadialChart | SingleStackedBarChart | ScatterChart | AreaChart | BarChart | LineChart | Table | TagBlock | Form | Buttons | IconButton | Steps | Timeline | Checklist | EntityList | EditableTable | ValueCard | ValueLayout | InsightCard | CompositeCardBlock | ImageCard)[], leading?: Icon | Avatar | Emoji)
TabItem.description: One tab: TabItem(value, trigger, content, leading?), e.g. TabItem("growth", "User growth", [growthChart], Icon("trending-up", "charts")). value is a unique id; trigger is the short pill label, one to three words; content is what the tab shows. leading is optional: an Icon per view, an inline Avatar (with an icon) for a person's tab, or an Emoji only in rare expressive content. Give every tab a leading or none of them.

Accordion.description: Collapsible items for supplementary detail the reader opens on demand, most often an FAQ: Accordion([item1, item2, item3]). Keep it to 3–5 items and place it last in its Section or Card; never hide primary information in it. For topics that are equally prominent parts of a long report use SectionBlock, and for alternative views use Tabs.

AccordionItem.signature: AccordionItem(value: string, trigger: string, content: (Text | Markdown | Link | Metric | Avatar | AvatarStack | Heading | LeadingText | EntityTitle | ImageTitle | Callout | CodeBlock | Image | ImageGallery | Separator | HorizontalBarChart | RadarChart | PieChart | RadialChart | SingleStackedBarChart | ScatterChart | AreaChart | BarChart | LineChart | Table | TagBlock | Form | Buttons | IconButton | Steps | Timeline | Checklist | EntityList | EditableTable | ValueCard | ValueLayout | InsightCard | CompositeCardBlock | ImageCard)[], leading?: Icon | Avatar | Emoji)
AccordionItem.description: One collapsible item: AccordionItem(value, trigger, content, leading?), e.g. AccordionItem("refunds", "Can I get a refund?", [Markdown("Yes, within 30 days of purchase.")], Icon("receipt", "finance")). value is a unique id; trigger is the title the reader clicks, a short question or topic; content is what opens. leading is optional: an Icon for a topic, an inline Avatar (with an icon) for the person who owns that item, or an Emoji only in rare expressive content. Give every item a leading or none of them.

Steps.description: A numbered how-to: Steps([StepsItem(Text("Install the CLI", "body", true), "Run npm i -g @openuidev/cli."), StepsItem(Text("Log in", "body", true), "Run openui login and follow the browser prompt.")]). Each step gets a 1, 2, 3 number chip automatically, so never number the titles yourself. Use it for instructions the reader carries out in order. For events in time order (an itinerary, schedule, history or tracking) use Timeline; for ranked picks or options use ListBlock.

StepsItem.signature: StepsItem(title: string | Text | Link | Tag | (string | Text | Link | Tag)[], subtitle?: string | Text | Metric | Tag | TagBlock | LeadingText | Link | (string | Text | Metric | Tag | TagBlock | LeadingText | Link)[])
StepsItem.description: One numbered step: StepsItem(title, subtitle?). title is the action in a few words: a string, or a Text, Link or Tag; there is no emphasis option, so to emphasize the title pass Text("Install the CLI", "body", true). subtitle is one or two plain sentences (not Markdown) on how to do it: a string, or a Text, Metric, Tag, TagBlock, LeadingText or Link. When title or subtitle needs two or more pieces side by side, pass an array.

Carousel.signature: Carousel(children: (Card | Image | CompositeCardItem | ImageCardItem | InsightCardItem | ValueCardItem)[])
Carousel.description: Horizontal scrollable row of 2+ slides the reader browses sideways. Every slide is the same type, one of: Card (its variant sets the look; keep every Card the same variant and shape, e.g. Carousel([Card([...]), Card([...])])); Image (a photo strip; give every Image the same aspectRatio so they line up); or one kind of card item, CompositeCardItem, ImageCardItem, InsightCardItem or ValueCardItem, which render exactly as in their block's carousel layout, e.g. Carousel([ImageCardItem(...), ImageCardItem(...)]). Which to use: a set of one card type with one shared click action uses that block's own carousel layout, e.g. ImageCard([lm1, lm2, lm3], "carousel", true, action) or ValueCard([v1, v2, v3], "vertical", true, null, null, true), which keeps the shared action. Use Carousel for slides of custom Cards or Images, or for card items that need no shared action.

TagBlock.description: tags is an array of strings, each shown as a 24px Tag pill

Tag.signature: Tag(text: string, leading?: Icon | Avatar | Emoji | Shape, variant?: "neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "purple" | "pink" | "inverted")
Tag.description: A 24px pill: Tag(text, leading?, variant?). leading is an optional Icon for a concept, a Shape for a status dot or category marker (Tag("Online", Shape("circle", "success"))), an Avatar for a person or company, or an Emoji in rare expressive content. Pick variant by meaning: "success" positive, "danger" negative, "warning" cautionary, "info" informational, "neutral" (default) a plain label; "purple" and "pink" only to tell categories apart; "inverted" for a single high-emphasis label. Pass null for leading to set just a variant: Tag("Open", null, "success").

Icon.description: A lucide line icon, named by its exact kebab-case lucide name: Icon("circle-check"), Icon("calendar"), Icon("map-pin"). It never stands alone: it fills the icon slot of another component (LeadingText, Tag, ChipItem, Avatar, EntityTitle, IconButton, OptionCard), and that host sets its size, stroke and color, so Icon has no size or color of its own. In LeadingText it scales with the Text (about 1.1–1.2em, 1.5 stroke) and takes the text's color. The name is looked up in lucide when it renders; an unknown or misspelled name shows a plain circle, so use only names you know exist and prefer common ones over guesses. category is optional and does not change the icon. Use Icon for a concept, fact or status; for a specific real person or company put an Avatar in the same slot.

EntityList.signature: EntityList(rows?: EntityListItem[], size?: "small" | "default", header?: EntityListItem, footer?: EntityListItem)
EntityList.description: A compact list of EntityListItem rows, each a left item and an optional right value: EntityListItem(left, right?, rightVariant?). Keep left a plain string for simple key/value facts, e.g. EntityListItem("Check-in", "3pm"). Use an EntityTitle on the left when each row is a person, company or product the reader should recognise, e.g. a team list or top customers, and a LeadingText when each row is a fact with an icon cue. right is a value string, a Metric (a number with a change), a Tag (a status) or a Text; leave it out for a plain list of entities. rightVariant "number" lines up string numbers with tabular figures. size "default" supports an optional header row for column labels and a footer row for a total, both EntityListItems; "small" has neither and is only for a CompositeCardItem body. When a left or right cell needs two or more pieces side by side, pass an array and they sit on one line, e.g. EntityListItem("Trail Runner", [Metric("$89", null, null, "sm"), Tag("In stock", null, "success")]); a single piece goes in directly.

EntityListItem.signature: EntityListItem(left: string | EntityTitle | LeadingText | (string | EntityTitle | LeadingText)[], right?: string | Metric | Tag | Text | (string | Metric | Tag | Text)[], rightVariant?: "text" | "number")
EntityListItem.description: One row of an EntityList: EntityListItem(left, right?, rightVariant?), e.g. EntityListItem("Check-in", "3pm"). left is a plain string for a key/value fact, an EntityTitle for a person, company or product, a LeadingText for a fact with an icon, or an array of these when it needs two pieces side by side. right is an optional value: a string, a Metric for a number with its change, a Tag for a status, a Text, or an array of these shown on one line; leave it out for a plain list of entities. rightVariant "number" lines up string numbers with tabular figures; a Metric doesn't need it. The same item also serves as the EntityList header (column labels, e.g. EntityListItem("Item", "Price")) and footer (a total, e.g. EntityListItem("Total", "$142.50", "number")).

ListBlock.description: A vertical list of ListItems for a set of options, picks or ranked results: ListBlock([item1, item2, item3]). variant "number" (default) puts a small black number inline before each title, for rankings, ordered picks or a short sequence; "plain" drops the numbers, for an unordered set such as people, companies or places that each lead with an Avatar. For named steps or options with a description, give each ListItem an emphasized title, ListItem(Text("Read the docs", "body", true), "Skim the quickstart."). Use Steps for a step-by-step process and EntityList for key/value facts. Give each ListItem an action to turn the list into a menu of follow-ups, or an actionSlot Button when each row needs its own verb such as Book or Approve.

ListItem.signature: ListItem(title: string | Text | Link | Tag | (string | Text | Link | Tag)[], subtitle?: string | Text | Metric | Tag | TagBlock | LeadingText | Link | (string | Text | Metric | Tag | TagBlock | LeadingText | Link)[], leading?: Avatar | Icon | Emoji, actionLabel?: string, action?: ActionExpression, actionSlot?: Button | Buttons | IconButton)
ListItem.description: One row in a ListBlock: ListItem(title, subtitle?, leading?, actionLabel?, action?, actionSlot?). title is a string, or a Text, Link or Tag. For a step or option with a name plus a description, emphasize the name with the "body" Text variant (it lines up with the number) and put the description in subtitle: ListItem(Text("Read the docs", "body", true), "Skim the quickstart and the component reference."). subtitle is one line of context: a string, or a Text, Metric, Tag, TagBlock, LeadingText or Link. leading is an optional Avatar (a real photo, a company logo via domain, or a tinted icon badge), an Icon, or a rare Emoji; it is 40px when the list has subtitles and 24px otherwise, and fits best in a "plain" list since numbered rows already lead with their number. The row is clickable only when it has an action (5th argument), e.g. ListItem("Cherry blossoms at Parc de Sceaux", "March – May", null, null, @ToAssistant("Tell me about cherry blossom season in Paris")); actionLabel is an optional short word shown at the right next to the chevron, e.g. "View". Use action for a whole-row drill-in like that. For an explicit verb, put real controls on the right with actionSlot (6th argument), a Button, a Buttons group or an IconButton, e.g. ListItem("Septime", "Tonight · 8:30pm", null, null, null, Button("Book", @ToAssistant("Book Septime tonight at 8:30pm"), "secondary")), or Buttons with Approve and Decline. With actionSlot the row itself is not clickable, so leave action and actionLabel out. When title or subtitle needs two or more pieces side by side, pass an array and they sit on one line, e.g. subtitle [Metric("$89", null, null, "sm"), Tag("In stock", null, "success")]; a single piece goes in directly.

Timeline.description: Events in time order along a dashed rail: an itinerary, a schedule, order status, a project history or an activity log. Timeline([TimelineItem("Check in", "Hotel Lutetia", "3:00 PM"), TimelineItem(Text("Dinner", "body", true), "Septime · table for 2", "8:30 PM")]). Give every item a time when the moments are known; use status to show progress through a plan. Use Steps for how-to instructions and ListBlock for an unordered set.

TimelineItem.signature: TimelineItem(title: string | Text | Link | Tag | (string | Text | Link | Tag)[], subtitle?: string | Text | Metric | Tag | TagBlock | LeadingText | Link | (string | Text | Metric | Tag | TagBlock | LeadingText | Link)[], time?: string | Text | Tag | (string | Text | Tag)[], leading?: Avatar | Icon | Emoji, status?: "done" | "current" | "upcoming")
TimelineItem.description: One event in a Timeline: TimelineItem(title, subtitle?, time?, leading?, status?). title is a string, or a Text, Link or Tag; emphasize a named event with Text("Doors open", "body", true). subtitle is one line of context: a string, or a Text, Metric, Tag, TagBlock, LeadingText or Link. time is when it happens, shown in a column on the left: a short string such as "9:00 AM", "Day 2" or "Mar 2024", or a Text or Tag. leading is an optional Avatar, Icon or Emoji that replaces the dot, e.g. Avatar("Priya Shah", null, null, null, "inline", Icon("user", "people")) for who acted. status "done" fills the dot, "current" highlights it, "upcoming" quiets the title; leave it out for a plain history. When title or subtitle needs two or more pieces side by side, pass an array.

Checklist.signature: Checklist(items: ChecklistItem[], name?: string, value?: $binding<Record<string, boolean>>)
Checklist.description: A list of items with round checks: Checklist(items, name?, value?), e.g. Checklist([ChecklistItem("Book flights", "Paris, Mar 12–19", true, "flights"), ChecklistItem("Reserve hotel", "Saint-Germain, 7 nights", false, "hotel"), ChecklistItem("Get travel insurance", null, false, "insurance")], "trip-prep"). On its own the user can tick it: clicking a row, or pressing Space or Enter, toggles it, and checked rows strike through in secondary. checked on an item is its starting state. Give the Checklist a name, or bind value to a $variable holding { itemValue: boolean }, when the ticks should be kept or read back; without either, ticks live only on screen. Inside a CompositeCardItem body it is read-only, so use it there for what a plan or tier includes (checked true) or what is already done. Use it for packing lists, launch or onboarding checklists and to-dos. Use Steps for numbered instructions done in order and Timeline for time-ordered events.

ChecklistItem.signature: ChecklistItem(title: string | Text | Link | Tag | (string | Text | Link | Tag)[], subtitle?: string | Text | Metric | Tag | TagBlock | LeadingText | Link | (string | Text | Metric | Tag | TagBlock | LeadingText | Link)[], checked?: boolean, value?: string)
ChecklistItem.description: One item in a Checklist: ChecklistItem(title, subtitle?, checked?, value?). title is the task, a string or a Text, Link or Tag. subtitle is one line of context: a string, or a Text, Metric, Tag, TagBlock, LeadingText or Link. checked true starts it ticked; leave it out for items still to do. value is the key the tick is stored under in the Checklist value, such as "flights"; give every item one when the Checklist has a name or value. When title or subtitle needs two or more pieces side by side, pass an array.

ValueCardItem.signature: ValueCardItem(id?: string, title: string, subtitle?: string | Text | Metric | Tag | LeadingText | Link | (string | Text | Metric | Tag | LeadingText | Link)[], leading?: Avatar | Icon | Emoji, value?: Metric | Text | Tag | TagBlock | LeadingText | (Metric | Text | Tag | TagBlock | LeadingText)[])
ValueCardItem.description: One card in a ValueCard: ValueCardItem(id?, title, subtitle?, leading?, value?). title says what the value is; subtitle adds a short context line (a string, or a Text, Metric, Tag, LeadingText or Link, or an array of them on one line); leading is an optional Avatar (a photo, logo or tinted icon badge), Icon or Emoji. In a horizontal card with a subtitle, the title stacks over the subtitle beside a 36px leading (an Avatar fills it, a bare Icon becomes a neutral badge) and the value sits on the right; without a subtitle the leading sits inline before the title like a LeadingText. In a vertical card the leading and title share one line, the subtitle sits under the title, and the hero value follows below. value is a Metric, Text, Tag, TagBlock or LeadingText, or an array of them on one line.

ValueCard.signature: ValueCard(items: ValueCardItem[], layout?: "horizontal" | "vertical", responsive?: boolean, action?: ActionExpression, gap?: number | string, carousel?: boolean)
ValueCard.description: A responsive grid of 2 or more compact cards, each one short fact or KPI: ValueCard([item1, item2, item3], layout?, responsive?, action?, gap?, carousel?). Each card is a ValueCardItem(id?, title, subtitle?, leading?, value?), e.g. ValueCardItem("revenue", "Revenue", "Month to date", Icon("circle-dollar-sign", "finance"), Metric("$48,200", "+8.1%", null, "sm")). Set layout once on the ValueCard for the whole group, never per item. Use "horizontal" only when every value is a single short piece (one Metric or a short Text); if any value has more, such as a Metric plus a Tag or a Metric plus a Text note, use "vertical" for the whole block. "horizontal" (default) is for key/value facts: the value goes on the right, with a Metric at "sm"; with a subtitle the title stacks over it beside a 36px leading (an Avatar fills it, a bare Icon becomes a neutral badge), and without one the leading sits inline before the title like a LeadingText. "vertical" is for KPI tiles where the number is the hero: the leading and title sit on one line, the subtitle on its own line under the title, and the value goes below at the default size, e.g. ValueCard([v1, v2, v3], "vertical", true). leading is an Icon for a concept, or an Avatar for a person or company with a real photo or logo. carousel (vertical only) scrolls the cards sideways instead of wrapping, for secondary browsing. Every item uses the same parts. action is one shared action for all cards, with the clicked card's details attached, so keep its @ToAssistant message generic and never use @OpenUrl. Use ValueCard for dashboard-like output, such as an analytics or monitoring view; for an inline section of figures inside a normal response use ValueLayout instead. For a long list of key/value rows use EntityList; for one headline figure use a Metric on its own.

ValueLayout.signature: ValueLayout(items: ValueCardItem[], layout?: "horizontal" | "vertical", responsive?: boolean, gap?: number | string, carousel?: boolean)
ValueLayout.description: A lighter ValueCard: the same ValueCardItems, laid out in a grid or carousel with dashed rules between them instead of tinted cards. ValueLayout([item1, item2, item3], layout?, responsive?, gap?, carousel?), e.g. ValueLayout([ValueCardItem("revenue", "Revenue", "Month to date", Icon("circle-dollar-sign", "finance"), Metric("$48,200", "+8.1%", null, "sm")), ValueCardItem("orders", "Orders", "Month to date", Icon("shopping-cart", "shopping"), Metric("1,204", "+3.4%", null, "sm"))]). It follows every ValueCard rule: 2 or more items of the same shape, layout set once on the group, "horizontal" only when every value is one short piece and "vertical" otherwise, and carousel for vertical only. It has no action: it is informational only, so use ValueCard if the figures must be clickable. Use ValueLayout as an inline section of figures inside a normal UI response, such as key numbers in an answer about a company, city or product, where tinted cards would feel heavy. Use ValueCard for dashboard-like output, such as an analytics or monitoring view.

InsightCardItem.signature: InsightCardItem(id?: string, title: string, subtitle?: string | Text | Metric | Tag | LeadingText | Link | (string | Text | Metric | Tag | LeadingText | Link)[], overline?: string, leading?: Avatar | Icon | Emoji, color?: "neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "purple" | "pink" | "inverted")
InsightCardItem.description: One tall insight tile: InsightCardItem(id?, title, subtitle?, overline?, leading?, color?), e.g. InsightCardItem("remote-work", "Hybrid roles are 52% of new postings", Tag("Rising", null, "success"), "Remote work", Icon("trending-up", "charts"), "info"). overline is the short label at the top, the topic or category in one to three words, with the optional leading (an Icon, Avatar or Emoji) before it. title is the insight itself, shown large at the bottom (22px), so keep it to one short sentence or phrase; it is plain text, never a Tag. subtitle sits under the title: a string, or a Text, Metric, Tag, LeadingText or Link, or an array of them on one line, such as a status Tag or a source Link. color picks a tint from the palette only, "neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "purple" | "pink" | "inverted", and the text takes the matching colour; pick it by meaning like Tag variants, use "neutral" when nothing calls for meaning, and never invent other colours. For a tile with a real photo behind the text, use ImageCard instead.

InsightCard.signature: InsightCard(items: InsightCardItem[], layout?: "grid" | "carousel", responsive?: boolean, action?: ActionExpression, gap?: number | string)
InsightCard.description: A grid or carousel of 2 or more tall tiles, each one takeaway: InsightCard([item1, item2, item3], layout?, responsive?, action?, gap?). Each tile has a short overline (the topic) at the top and the insight as a large title at the bottom. Use it for key takeaways from research, trends or news (with a status Tag in each subtitle), topics to explore as entry points, plan options, or suggested next topics after an answer. layout "grid" (default) for the main side-by-side set, "carousel" for secondary browsing. Keep every item the same shape, with the same kind of subtitle. Tiles have no photo; for photo tiles use ImageCard. action is one shared action for every tile, with the clicked tile's details attached and hover and press feedback added automatically, so keep its @ToAssistant message generic (e.g. "Tell me more about this trend") and never use @OpenUrl. For figures use ValueCard or ValueLayout; for products with a price and a button use CompositeCardBlock.

CompositeCardItem.signature: CompositeCardItem(id?: string, header?: EntityTitle | ImageTitle | Text | Image | LeadingText, body?: (Text | Metric | EntityTitle | Image | AreaChart | BarChart | LineChart | ListBlock | TagBlock | EntityList | Checklist)[], footer?: {price?: Metric, button?: Button | Buttons | IconButton | IconButton[]}, media?: Image | AreaChart | BarChart | LineChart)
CompositeCardItem.description: One rich white card: CompositeCardItem(id?, header?, body?, footer?, media?), e.g. CompositeCardItem("widget-pro", EntityTitle(Icon("package", "shopping"), "Widget Pro", "Best seller"), [Text("Sold this month"), Metric("2,410 units", "+12%", null, "sm")], { price: Metric("$29.00"), button: Button("View details", @ToAssistant("Show details for Widget Pro"), "secondary") }). header is an EntityTitle for a named product, company or person, an ImageTitle or Image for a real photo, or a Text title as Text("…", "h3"). body stacks the content: Text renders as 14px body copy (secondary unless emphasis is true), Metric at size "sm", EntityTitle, Image, a chart, ListBlock, TagBlock, a small EntityList, or a Checklist for what is included or done (pricing tiers, onboarding, launch readiness), which beats a ListBlock with check icons. footer holds an optional price Metric, always shown at 18px so it needs no size (pass previous for a sale), and a Button; for two actions use Buttons([primary, secondary], "column"), which stacks them full width. For compact actions, pass one IconButton or an array of them instead; they sit in a row to the right of the price. Each must open a real page (@OpenUrl) or ask a real follow-up (@ToAssistant), never a save, share or cart action the app cannot do, e.g. { price: Metric("$179"), button: [IconButton("Show similar", Icon("search"), @ToAssistant("Show headphones similar to Studio Headphones"), "secondary"), IconButton("Open product page", Icon("external-link"), @OpenUrl("https://…"), "secondary")] }. A footer Button can open the card's own real page with @OpenUrl. media (5th) is a real photo, with a URL from a tool result or the user and never invented, shown edge to edge across the top of the card, above the header: CompositeCardItem("lutetia", Text("Hôtel Lutetia", "h3"), [Text("Art Deco landmark on the Left Bank.")], { price: Metric("€420 / night"), button: Button("Book", @ToAssistant("Book Hôtel Lutetia"), "primary") }, Image("Hôtel Lutetia", "https://…", "16:9")). Prefer media over an Image header when the card leads with a photo. media can instead be an AreaChart, BarChart or LineChart for a compact trend across the top of a metric or trend card, such as MRR over six months or weekly signups, e.g. CompositeCardItem("mrr", Text("MRR · last 6 months", "h3"), [Metric("$84.2k", "+12%", null, "sm")], null, AreaChart(["May", "Jun", "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct"], [Series("MRR", [52, 58, 61, 66, 75, 84])])). Keep one strong block per card: never stack two big-hierarchy blocks together, such as an EntityTitle header (with its 44px badge) next to media, a chart, an ImageTitle or a large Metric. When the card already has a hero like a photo or chart, title it with a plain Text, or a LeadingText such as LeadingText(Icon("dollar-sign", "finance"), Text("MRR", "body", true)) when an icon helps, instead of an EntityTitle.

CompositeCardBlock.signature: CompositeCardBlock(items: CompositeCardItem[], layout?: "grid" | "carousel", responsive?: boolean, action?: ActionExpression, gap?: number | string)
CompositeCardBlock.description: The fallback card block: use it only when no specialised card fits, so first reach for ImageCard (photo tiles), InsightCard (takeaways), ValueCard or ValueLayout (figures), EntityList or ListBlock (rows), or OptionCards (choices in a form). A two-per-row grid or carousel of 2 or more rich cards, for products, offers, plans or deep-dive topics that need more than a title and a line, such as a header, mixed body content and a price or button footer: CompositeCardBlock([item1, item2], layout?, responsive?, action?, gap?). layout "grid" (default) for side-by-side comparison, "carousel" for secondary browsing. Every card uses the same parts in the same order. action is one shared action for every card, with the clicked card's details attached, so keep its @ToAssistant message generic and never use @OpenUrl there; give each card its own link with a footer Button instead. For short facts use ValueCard or ValueLayout; for photo tiles use ImageCard.

ImageCardItem.signature: ImageCardItem(id?: string, src: string, title: string, subtitle?: string | Text | Metric | Tag | LeadingText | Link | (string | Text | Metric | Tag | LeadingText | Link)[], overline?: string, leading?: Avatar | Icon | Emoji, alt?: string, actions?: IconButton | IconButton[])
ImageCardItem.description: One tall photo tile: ImageCardItem(id?, src, title, subtitle?, overline?, leading?, alt?, actions?), e.g. ImageCardItem("eiffel-tower", "https://…/eiffel.jpg", "Eiffel Tower", ["Open daily 9am–midnight", Tag("Must-See", null, "info")], null, null, "Aerial view of the Eiffel Tower"). src is a real image URL from a tool result or the user, never invented, shown full-bleed behind the text with dark gradients so the white text stays readable. overline is an optional short label at the top left (a category such as "Museum"), with leading (an Icon, Avatar or Emoji) before it. title (22px) is the name of the place or item, and subtitle sits under it: a string, Text, Metric, Tag, LeadingText or Link, or an array of them on one line. actions are optional IconButtons at the top right, only for something that really happens: an @OpenUrl to the item's own page from a tool result, or a @ToAssistant follow-up such as IconButton("Hotels nearby", Icon("bed", "travel"), @ToAssistant("Show hotels near the Eiffel Tower")); never save, share or download, which you cannot perform. alt describes the photo.

ImageCard.signature: ImageCard(items: ImageCardItem[], layout?: "grid" | "carousel", responsive?: boolean, action?: ActionExpression, gap?: number | string)
ImageCard.description: A grid or carousel of 2 or more tall photo tiles for places, products, media or inspiration: ImageCard([item1, item2], layout?, responsive?, action?, gap?), e.g. ImageCard([lm1, lm2, lm3], "carousel", true, @ToAssistant("Tell me more about this Paris landmark")). Each tile is a real photo behind an overline (top left), optional IconButton actions (top right), and a title with a composable subtitle (bottom). Use it only when every item has a real image URL from a tool result or the user; with no real photos, use InsightCard. layout "grid" (default) for a main side-by-side set, "carousel" for secondary browsing. Keep every item the same shape. action is one shared action for every tile, with the clicked tile's details attached, so keep its @ToAssistant message generic and never use @OpenUrl there; IconButtons keep their own actions. For a single picture that illustrates an answer use Image, and for products with a price and a buy button use CompositeCardBlock.

Modal.signature: Modal(title: string, open?: $binding<boolean>, children: (Text | Markdown | Link | Metric | Avatar | AvatarStack | Heading | LeadingText | EntityTitle | ImageTitle | Callout | CodeBlock | Image | ImageGallery | Separator | HorizontalBarChart | RadarChart | PieChart | RadialChart | SingleStackedBarChart | ScatterChart | AreaChart | BarChart | LineChart | Table | TagBlock | Form | Buttons | IconButton | Steps | Timeline | Checklist | EntityList | EditableTable | ValueCard | ValueLayout | InsightCard | CompositeCardBlock | ImageCard)[], size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg")
Modal.description: Modal dialog. open is a reactive $boolean binding — set to true to open, X/Escape/backdrop auto-closes. Put Form with buttons inside children.

FollowUpBlock.description: List of clickable follow-up suggestions placed at the end of a response

FollowUpItem.description: Clickable follow-up suggestion — when clicked, sends text as user message

Sources.signature: Sources(items: {url?: string, title: string, sourceName: string}[])
Sources.description: Row of source cards (favicon, site name, page title) that closes an answer built from real references, e.g. Sources([{ title: "Apple (AAPL) Statistics & Valuation", sourceName: "Stock Analysis", url: "https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/aapl/statistics/" }]). Each item links to its url.

componentGroups.name: Layout
notes: - Shell(title, [children]) frames a dashboard or large Grid layout: a small title, an outline, wider than the chat column, with an expand button for full screen. At most one per response. Bleed([children]) is the same width with no frame, for a wide hero Image, comparison Grid or Carousel; wrap a Grid comparing an odd number of cards (3 or 5 plans) in a Bleed, Bleed([Grid([p1, p2, p3], 3)]), so they sit in one row instead of 2 + 1. Never nest either.

- For dashboards and equal columns use Grid(children, columns?): columns 2 (default) | 3 | 4, collapsing to fewer on narrow screens, e.g. a KPI row Grid([c1, c2, c3, c4], 4) above Grid([chartCard1, chartCard2]). Use a Stack row only for a few items of mixed width.
- Use nested Stacks when you need explicit rows/sections.

- Build every response from Sections: Section([children]) holds one part (an overview, then options, then next steps) with more space after it and tight spacing inside. Compose each part yourself: a Heading title first when it needs one, then content; rows or grids inside with Stack or card blocks. Never nested. Sections are high-level divisions and many responses have only one; never give a lone Text, Markdown, Buttons row or title (Heading or Text, with or without a subtitle) its own Section, so an intro or a dashboard header goes first inside the Section holding the content it introduces.
- Show/hide sections: $editId != "" ? Card([editForm]) : null
- Modal: Modal("Title", $showModal, [content]) — $showModal is boolean, X/Escape auto-closes. Put Form with its own buttons inside children.
- Use Tabs for alternative views (chart types, data sections) — no $variable needed
- Shared filter across Tabs: same $days binding in Query args works across all TabItems

componentGroups.name: Content
notes: - Metric(value, delta?, variant?, size?, previous?) is a value with an optional change (+/- shows an up/down arrow); label it with the Card title inside a Card, or compose one with Text or Heading elsewhere. It uses the UI font, so use size "sm" whenever it is not the hero number: Table cells, EntityListItem right, ListItem/EntityTitle subtitles, ImageTitle content, ValueCardItem value, CompositeCardItem body (a CompositeCardItem footer price always renders at 18px), e.g. Col("Change", @Each(data.rows, "r", Metric(r.value, r.change, "horizontal", "sm"))). Only a standalone headline figure gets "vertical", "large", e.g. Card([Metric("$48,200", "+8.1%", "vertical", "large")], null, "Revenue"). previous (5th) strikes through an earlier value for a real before/after, like a price drop: Metric("$89", "-26%", null, "sm", "$120").

- Avatar is a photo, logo or tinted icon badge that can stand in for an Icon (LeadingText, Tag, Chips): Avatar("Ada Lovelace", "https://…/ada.jpg", null, null, null, Icon("user", "people")) for a person, Avatar("Stripe", null, "rounded", "stripe.com", null, Icon("building-2", "business")) for a company logo, Avatar("Billing", null, "rounded", null, "md", Icon("credit-card", "finance"), "info") for a standalone concept badge. ALWAYS pass an icon, even with src or domain: it renders when the image is missing or broken. src must be a real URL; a person with no real photo URL gets Icon("user", "people") inside and no src. The icon slot also takes a Shape for a solid colored mark. A concept on a text line stays a plain Icon.

- Heading("Title", "Supporting line") titles a UI section when the description adds a fact the title lacks (scope, unit, time range, what to do). Never a description that greets, introduces you, restates the title or says what the section contains; a bare title is Text h2/h3.
- Greetings, small talk and short conversational replies are one plain Markdown block with no heading, Heading or Text title.

- EntityTitle(leading, title, subtitle) names a person, company, product, place or topic behind an Avatar-first leading visual (a photo, a domain logo or a tinted icon badge): EntityTitle(Avatar("Stripe", null, "rounded", "stripe.com", null, Icon("building-2", "business")), "Stripe", "Payments infrastructure"). subtitle is required: a string, or a Tag, Metric, Link, TagBlock or LeadingText for a status, price, source or labels. A title with no subtitle is a LeadingText. Heading titles a section.

- ImageTitle(Image(alt, src, ratio), [content]) is one item in a grid or Carousel of 2+ products, articles or places: image on top, then a short content stack, usually a title Text("…", "body", true) (an EntityTitle only for a real person, brand or seller with their own photo or logo, never an icon Avatar), then one secondary line (an article author as a LeadingText with an inline Avatar and tone "secondary", a price Metric, Tags). Keep every item the same shape and ratio; a single illustrative picture is Image plus Markdown. Real image URLs only.

- LeadingText(leading, Text(...)) puts an Icon, Avatar or AvatarStack before any Text, centered on its first line: Icon for a concept or fact (LeadingText(Icon("calendar", "time"), Text("Opens daily 9am–6pm"))), Shape for a status dot, legend marker or trend triangle (LeadingText(Shape("triangle-up", "success"), Text("+12% this week"))), Avatar for one real person or company, AvatarStack for a group of them, and rarely an Emoji for expressive generated content (never in UI chrome). Avatars here use size "inline".

- AvatarStack([a1, a2, a3, a4, a5], 3) overlaps 2+ Avatars with a count chip for the rest: a team, attendees, who replied. Keep max at 3–5, set size on the stack, and name the group in Text beside it.
- Markdown is for explanations and the top-level prose that sets context around UI. Text is for short UI text: headings, labels, captions, single values.

- Answering a question with a title and prose: one Markdown block with a # heading, not Text h1 + Markdown. Text headings title UI (dashboards, forms, card groups); a part of a longer multi-part response is a Section that starts with a Heading.

- Callout("warning", "**Visa required.** Apply 3 weeks ahead.") is an icon (or a rare Emoji) plus short Markdown content for one standout aside (tip, caveat, warning, result), with no title. Pick variant by meaning; one or two per response at most; never for notes about what you did.
- Highlight in Markdown with ==key phrase==: a soft green marker behind the text.
- Use it for the one phrase that directly answers the question, at most 1-2 per response. Never for whole sentences, headings, links or code.
- Links: in Markdown write [descriptive text](https://…); the site's favicon renders before the link text automatically. Never use a bare URL as link text.

- For a standalone link outside prose (a source, docs or product page), use Link("Page name", "https://…"). When a Link is the title of a ListItem, StepsItem or TimelineItem, pass size "lg" so it matches the title size: Link("Septime", "https://…", "lg").

- Use Cards to group related KPIs or blocks: variant "outlined" (default) for ordinary groups, "lifted" for the one block that should stand out, "sunk" for secondary or nested content. For grouping without a frame use Stack; Stack with direction "row" for side-by-side layouts. A Card's children stack on their own; for a row or custom spacing inside a Card, pass one Stack child, e.g. Card([Stack([chartA, chartB], "row", "m")]).

- Success toast: Callout("success", "**Saved.** Your changes are live.", $showSuccess) — use @Set($showSuccess, true) in save action, auto-dismisses after 3s. For errors: result.status == "error" ? Callout("error", result.error) : null
- KPI card: Card([Metric("" + @Count(@Filter(data.rows, "field", "==", "value")), null, "vertical", "large")], null, "Label")

componentGroups.name: Tables
notes: - EditableTable(name, [EditableCol(key, label, type?, options?, icon?)], rows) lets the user edit cells inline. type is the cell editor: "text" (default), "number", "date", "select" (options as SelectItems) or "url"; each column shows a leading header icon for its type unless you pass an Icon.
- rows is an array of value arrays in column order (dates as ISO strings, selects as the SelectItem value). Edited data is submitted when the user clicks Save Changes.
- Table is COLUMN-oriented: Table([Col("Label", dataArray), Col("Count", countArray, "number")]). Use array pluck for data: data.rows.fieldName
- Col data can be component arrays for styled cells: Col("Status", @Each(data.rows, "item", Tag(item.status, null, item.status == "open" ? "success" : "danger")))
- Row actions: Col("Actions", @Each(data.rows, "t", Button("Edit", Action([@Set($showEdit, true), @Set($editId, t.id)]))))
- Sortable: sorted = @Sort(data.rows, $sortField, "desc"). Bind $sortField to Select. Use sorted.fieldName for Col data
- Searchable: filtered = @Filter(data.rows, "title", "contains", $search). Bind $search to Input
- Chain sort + filter: filtered = @Filter(...) then sorted = @Sort(filtered, ...) — use sorted for both Table and Charts
- Empty state: @Count(data.rows) > 0 ? Table([...]) : Text("No data yet")

componentGroups.name: Charts (2D)
notes: - Charts accept column arrays: LineChart(labels, [Series("Name", values)]). Use array pluck: LineChart(data.rows.day, [Series("Views", data.rows.views)])

- Use Cards to wrap charts, titled with the Card title and subtitle args, e.g. Card([chart], null, "Revenue by month", "Jul–Sep"), never a Heading or Text title inside the Card, but never wrap a Table or EditableTable in a Card: tables draw their own frame, so they sit directly in a Section or TabItem.
- Chart + Table from same source: use @Sort or @Filter result for both LineChart and Table Col data
- Multiple chart views: use Tabs — Tabs([TabItem("line", "Line", [LineChart(...)]), TabItem("bar", "Bar", [BarChart(...)])])

componentGroups.name: Charts (1D)
notes: - PieChart and BarChart need NUMBERS, not objects. For list data, use @Count(@Filter(...)) to aggregate:

- PieChart from list: `PieChart(["Low", "Med", "High"], [@Count(@Filter(data.rows, "priority", "==", "low")), @Count(@Filter(data.rows, "priority", "==", "medium")), @Count(@Filter(data.rows, "priority", "==", "high"))], "donut")`
- KPI from count: `Metric("" + @Count(@Filter(data.rows, "status", "==", "open")), null, "vertical", "large")`

componentGroups.name: Forms
notes: - Chips: compact single/multiple selection pills. Use ChipItem references for each option.
